serestar.title: Ser vs Estar
serestar.sub: The two «to be» — infinite rounds with explanations
items: State/condition right now → estar. The coffee isn't cold by identity.
The coffee is cold, shall I heat it up?
El perro ___ cansado después del paseo.
The dog is tired after the walk.
Taste right now → estar rico. Ser rico = wealthy!
Events take SER for location (where it takes place).
The party is at our house.
The stroller is in the hallway.
Ser listo = clever (trait). Estar listo = ready!
Estar listo = ready. Ser listo = clever.
The supermarket is closed on Sundays.
Estar malo = sick. Ser malo = a bad person!
The kid is a bit sick today.
Characteristic trait of the neighborhood → ser.
The door is open, close it.
El vino griego ___ mejor de lo que pensaba.
Greek wine is better than I thought.
El bebé ___ muy grande para su edad.
The baby is very big for his age.
Ser aburrido = boring. Estar aburrido = bored.
The movie is boring; I fell asleep.
El perro ___ aburrido; vamos al parque.
The dog is bored; let's go to the park.

porpara.title: Por vs Para
porpara.sub: Forward (para) or because/through (por) — with the why
items: This gift is for the baby.
I bought it for twenty euros.
Estudio español ___ hablar con mi suegra.
I study Spanish to talk with my mother-in-law.
We leave for Greece on Saturday.
Trabajo desde casa dos días ___ semana.
I work from home two days per week.
___ mí, el mejor bar es el de la esquina.
For me, the best bar is the one on the corner.
Lo hice ___ ti, porque te quiero.
Because of/for the sake of → por.
I did it for you (because of you), because I love you.
Hice esta tarta ___ ti; es tu regalo.
Destined to be received by you → para.
I made this cake for you; it's your gift.
We talk by phone every Sunday.
I work for a data company.
El perro entró ___ la puerta del jardín.
The dog came in through the garden gate.
I traded my car for a bike.
I need a babysitter for Saturday.
We lived in Ohio for three years.
El parque está bien ___ jugar con el perro.
The park is good for playing with the dog.
___ ser tan pequeño, el frenchie come muchísimo.
For being so small, the frenchie eats a ton.
We couldn't sleep because of the heat.
Is there anything to eat in the fridge?
La receta fue escrita ___ mi abuela.
The recipe was written by my grandmother.
Voy al mercado; te llamo ___ si necesitas algo.
Set phrase: por si (acaso) = in case.
I'm going to the market; I'll call you in case you need anything.
Queda pan ___ dos días como mucho.
There's bread left for two days at most.
A toast: to the future in Barcelona!

pasados.title: The Two Pasts
items: Ayer ___ (comí / comía) paella con unos amigos.
Yesterday I ate paella with some friends.
Ongoing background situation in childhood → imperfecto.
As a kid I lived in Ohio.
El bebé ___ (durmió / dormía) cuando llegué a casa.
Scene in progress interrupted by an event → imperfecto.
The baby was sleeping when I got home.
'De repente' = a sudden completed event → pretérito.
Antes ___ (fuimos / íbamos) a la playa todos los veranos.
We used to go to the beach every summer.
One completed trip, closed time frame → pretérito.
___ (Hizo / Hacía) un sol precioso y el mar estaba en calma.
The sun was beautiful and the sea was calm.
Anoche el niño se ___ (despertó / despertaba) tres veces.
Last night the kid woke up three times.
Cuando ___ (tuve / tenía) veinte años, no cocinaba nada.
When I was twenty, I didn't cook at all.
Ayer ___ (conocí / conocía) a los padres de mi mujer.
Conocí = I met (first time). Conocía = I already knew.
Yesterday I met my wife's parents.
No ___ (supe / sabía) que hablabas español tan bien.
Sabía = I (didn't) know, ongoing state. Supe = found out.
I didn't know you spoke Spanish so well.
Cuando vi la factura, ___ (supe / sabía) que había un error.
Supe = I realized/found out at that moment.
When I saw the bill, I knew (realized) there was a mistake.
I arrived, had dinner, and went to bed.
Mientras yo ___ (cociné / cocinaba), el perro vigilaba la cocina.
While I was cooking, the dog was watching the kitchen.
El lunes ___ (empezó / empezaba) a llover a las cinco.
Beginning of an action at a set time → pretérito.
On Monday it started raining at five.
La casa de mis abuelos ___ (fue / era) blanca y enorme.
My grandparents' house was white and huge.
___ (Fueron / Eran) las dos cuando por fin se durmió.
Clock time in the past → imperfecto (eran las dos).
It was two o'clock when he finally fell asleep.
Ayer no ___ (quise / quería) salir: estaba agotado.
Quería = ongoing desire/state. Quise = tried; no quise = refused.
Yesterday I didn't want to go out: I was exhausted.
Se lo pedí, pero no ___ (quiso / quería) ayudarme.
No quiso = he refused (a decision, completed).
I asked him, but he refused to help me.
Siempre ___ (pedimos / pedíamos) bravas en ese bar.
We always used to order bravas at that bar.
El sábado ___ (probé / probaba) el vermut por primera vez.
On Saturday I tried vermouth for the first time.
El bar ___ (estuvo / estaba) lleno y olía a jamón.
The bar was packed and smelled of ham.
We managed to park right in front: a miracle!
De pequeño no ___ (pude / podía) comer gluten.
As a kid I couldn't eat gluten.
La semana pasada el frenchie ___ (rompió / rompía) su juguete favorito.
Last week the frenchie broke his favorite toy.

subjuntivo.title: Subjunctive or not?
subjuntivo.sub: Spot the triggers: wishes, doubts, emotions, cuando-future
items: Quiero que ___ (vienes / vengas) a la fiesta.
Querer que + different subject = influence trigger → subjunctive.
I want you to come to the party.
Creo que el restaurante ___ (es / sea) muy bueno.
I think the restaurant is very good.
No creo que ___ (es / sea) tan caro.
I don't think it's that expensive.
Espero que el bebé ___ (duerme / duerma) esta noche.
I hope the baby sleeps tonight.
It's possible it will rain tomorrow.
Cuando ___ (llego / llegue) a casa, te llamo.
When I get home, I'll call you.
Cuando ___ (llego / llegue) a casa, siempre saco al perro.
When I get home, I always take the dog out.
Te recomiendo que ___ (pruebas / pruebes) el pulpo.
I recommend you try the octopus.
Dudo que ___ (llegan / lleguen) antes de las nueve.
I doubt they'll arrive before nine.
Me alegro de que todo ___ (va / vaya) bien.
I'm glad everything is going well.
Hopefully it'll be sunny this weekend.
Busco un piso que ___ (tiene / tenga) terraza.
I'm looking for an apartment that has a terrace.
Vivo en un piso que ___ (tiene / tenga) mucha luz.
I live in an apartment that gets a lot of light.
Es importante que el perro ___ (bebe / beba) agua con este calor.
Es importante que = impersonal trigger → subjunctive.
It's important that the dog drinks water in this heat.
Aunque ___ (llueve / llueva), iremos a la playa.
Even if it rains, we'll go to the beach.
Aunque ___ (llueve / llueva) ahora mismo, no hace frío.
Aunque + observed fact (although it IS raining) → indicative.
Although it's raining right now, it's not cold.
Quiero ___ (ir / vaya) a Grecia este verano.
Same subject → infinitive (ir), no que, no subjunctive.
I want to go to Greece this summer.
Para que el bebé ___ (se duerme / se duerma), bajamos la luz.
So that the baby falls asleep, we dim the lights.
Dile a tu hermano que me ___ (llama / llame).
Tell your brother to call me.
Me parece que la película ___ (empieza / empiece) a las ocho.
I think the movie starts at eight.
No es verdad que los españoles ___ (duermen / duerman) siesta cada día.
It's not true that Spaniards nap every day.
En cuanto ___ (termino / termine) el informe, nos vamos de tapas.
As soon as I finish the report, we're going for tapas.
Antes de que ___ (se despierta / se despierte) el niño, tomemos el café.
Before the kid wakes up, let's have our coffee.

saberconocer.title: Saber vs Conocer
saberconocer.sub: Two ways «to know» — facts vs familiarity
items: I don't know where the keys are.
Do you know a good vet around here?
Saber + infinitive = to know how to.
My wife knows how to cook wonderfully.
Do you know the neighbors on the third floor?
Being familiar with a place → conocer.
¿___ a qué hora abre la farmacia?
Do you know what time the pharmacy opens?
___ Barcelona como la palma de mi mano.
Deep familiarity with a place → conocer.
I know Barcelona like the back of my hand.
The baby already knows how to say 'dad'.
Being acquainted with a story/topic → conocer.
Do you know the history of this neighborhood?
I don't know if it will rain tomorrow.
Experience a place for the first time → conocer.
I want my parents to get to know Spain.
Does anyone know the pediatrician's number?
___ un sitio con las mejores bravas de la ciudad.
I know a place with the best bravas in town.
Mi jefe no ___ que estoy aprendiendo español.
My boss doesn't know I'm learning Spanish.

perfectoindef.title: He comido vs Comí
perfectoindef.sub: The Spain perfect: open vs closed time frames
items: Hoy = open frame → Spain uses perfecto: he tomado/he comido.
Today I've had a lot of coffee.
Yesterday I ate paella at the beach.
Esta mañana (still today) → perfecto: he paseado.
This morning I walked the dog early.
La semana pasada ___ a mis suegros.
La semana pasada = closed → indefinido: visité.
Last week I visited my in-laws.
Have you ever tried Galician octopus?
Este año = still open → perfecto: he aprendido.
This year I've learned a lot of Spanish.
Hace + time = ago, closed → indefinido: fui.
Two days ago I went to the doctor.
Todavía no (yet) → perfecto: no he visitado.
I haven't visited the Sagrada Família yet.
Last night the kid slept terribly.
Esta semana = open frame → perfecto: has hablado.
Have you talked to your mom this week?
El lunes pasado = closed → indefinido: entregué.
Last Monday I handed in the report.
Nunca (in my life, so far) → perfecto: he visto.
I've never seen snow in Barcelona.
As a kid I lived in Ohio.
Just now, result in the present → perfecto: se me han quedado.
Oops! I've locked the keys inside.

muymucho.title: Muy vs Mucho
muymucho.sub: Very vs a lot — the eternal mixup
items: calor is a NOUN → mucho calor (never «muy calor»!).
hambre is a noun → mucha hambre.
I'm working a lot this week.
We're very lucky with this apartment.
There are a lot of people at the Boqueria.
Greek wine surprised me a lot.
We're very happy with the daycare.

quecual.title: Qué vs Cuál
quecual.sub: What vs which — not what you'd expect
items: Identification among options → cuál es (NOT qué es).
Definition (what IS this thing) → qué es.
Which do you prefer, wine or beer?
¿___ de estos bares te gusta más?
Which of these bars do you like most?
What kind of music do you listen to?
Data identification → cuál es tu dirección.
¿___ es la diferencia entre ser y estar?
Identifying the difference → cuál es la diferencia.
What's the difference between ser and estar?
Open 'what' with a verb → qué quieres.
What do you want to do today?
Favorite = picking among all dishes → cuál.
Preposition + qué + noun → en qué calle.
What street do you live on?
The classic: what's happening → qué pasa.

aende.title: A, En o De
aende.sub: The three little prepositions that run everything
items: Clock time of an event → a las nueve.
Es el carrito ___ el bebé... ¡del bebé!
I think about you every day.
I'm learning Spanish little by little.
Parts of the day → por/en la tarde (en also OK: en la tarde LatAm, por la tarde Spain — here en).
The flight leaves in the afternoon.
Range: de lunes a viernes → de... a.
Arriving TO a place → llegar a.
We arrive in Madrid on Saturday.
Entramos ___ el bar de la esquina.
We went into the corner bar.
I fell in love with this city.

eraestaba.title: Era vs Estaba
eraestaba.sub: Ser/estar, past edition — the double boss fight
items: La casa de mis abuelos ___ enorme.
Permanent trait described in the past → era.
When you called, I was in the shower.
El café ya ___ frío cuando volví.
The coffee was already cold when I got back.
Clock time in the past → always era/eran.
El bebé ___ dormido en el carrito.
The baby was asleep in the stroller.
La fiesta ___ en casa de Marta.
Events take ser for location → era.
The party was at Marta's place.
Yesterday I was exhausted after work.
De joven, mi padre ___ muy deportista.
When he was young, my dad was very athletic.
La puerta ___ abierta y el perro no ___... ¡se escapó!
The door was open and the dog was gone... he escaped!
___ un día precioso y decidimos ir a la playa.
Scene description of the day → era (hacía is also common).
It was a beautiful day and we decided to go to the beach.
Mi primer piso ___ pequeño pero acogedor.
Describing what it was like → era.
My first apartment was small but cozy.
Where were you when it all happened?
The soup was delicious — did you make it?
Su madre ___ enfermera antes de jubilarse.
Her mom was a nurse before retiring.

llevartraer.title: Llevar/Traer · Ir/Venir
llevartraer.sub: Direction verbs: it all depends on WHERE YOU ARE
items: ¿Puedes ___ el vino a la fiesta de Marta? (you'll both be there)
Movement AWAY from where you are now → llevar.
Can you take the wine to Marta's party?
¿Me puedes ___ un vaso de agua? (to me, here)
Can you bring me a glass of water?
Tomorrow I want to go to the beach.
¿Quieres ___ a mi casa esta tarde? (I'm at home)
Do you want to come to my place this evening?
Voy al súper, ¿te ___ algo? (back to you)
It returns to the listener/speaker → traer: ¿te traigo algo?
I'm going to the store — shall I bring you something?
Tenemos que ___ al perro al veterinario.
We have to take the dog to the vet.
Spanish says ¡ya voy! (I'm going toward you) — not vengo!
El lunes no puedo ___ a la reunión. (meeting is elsewhere)
Away from where you are → ir.
On Monday I can't go to the meeting.
¿A qué hora ___ tus padres a Barcelona? (we're in BCN)
Toward where the speaker is → venir.
What time do your parents arrive in Barcelona?
Bring it here with you → traer.
When you come, bring your swimsuit.
¿Me acompañas a ___ estas cajas al trastero?
Take away to another place → llevar.
Will you help me take these boxes to the storage room?
Waiter, can you bring us the check?
Este fin de semana nos ___ de excursión.
Set phrase irse de excursión → away → ir(se).
This weekend we're going on a day trip.
Who's taking the kid to school tomorrow?

pedirpreguntar.title: Pedir vs Preguntar
pedirpreguntar.sub: Asking FOR things vs asking questions
items: I'm going to order another beer.
Quiero ___ le si viene a la boda.
I want to ask him if he's coming to the wedding.
Can I ask you a favor?
Le voy a ___ al camarero qué lleva el plato.
I'm going to ask the waiter what's in the dish.
El niño no para de ___ agua.
The kid keeps asking for water.
___ por Marta cuando llegues; ella te abre.
Preguntar POR = ask for someone (at the door) → preguntar.
Ask for Marta when you arrive; she'll let you in.
Asking for info (a question) → preguntar. (pedir la dirección also heard, but the question-act → preguntar)
Can I ask you the vet's address?
Voy a ___ cita con el pediatra.
Pedir cita = book an appointment → pedir.
I'm going to book an appointment with the pediatrician.
Me ___ ó cuántos años llevaba en España.
He asked me a question → preguntó.
He asked me how long I'd been in Spain.
Have you apologized to your sister?
Nunca ___ ayuda, y ese es su problema.
He never asks for help, and that's his problem.
Si no lo sabes, ___ — no pasa nada.
If you don't know, ask — it's fine.
